pr_body:
Closes #40036

Prior to this commit POST requests with invalid parameters did not
consistently return 400 responses. In the case of a request with a
`_method` override, any invalid parameters prevent the [rack method
override middleware][] from determining the method override. At that
point the request comes into Rails as a POST request and the response
status depends on whether another route happens to match the POST
request.

In the case where a route happens to match the POST request, Rails
attempts to serve the request and then fails with
`ActionController::BadRequest` when referencing the invalid [request
parameters][]. This turns into a 400 response.

But if no route matches the POST request, Rails never gets far enough to
reference the invalid request parameters. Instead, the request fails
with `ActionController::RoutingError`, turning into a 404 response.
This is confusing, since it is a 404 for different route than we would
have expected to hit, given the `_method` override.

This commit ensures that we respond with a 400 status regardless of
whether an unrelated route happens to match. It does this by referencing
the parameters before passing the request off to Journey. If they are
invalid, referencing them will raise the `ActionController::BadRequest`,
triggering the 400 response.

Because this commit references the parameters earlier than before, it
also needs to set "rack.input" in the `ActionDispatch::RoutingVerbs`
test class to keep the tests green. In a real application I believe
"rack.input" should have already been set by the handler (see [Puma][],
for example).

[rack method override middleware]: https://github.com/rack/rack/blob/249dd785625f0cbe617d3144401de90ecf77025a/lib/rack/method_override.rb
[request parameters]: https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/7af59e16a255da5aee2863af0eefaa9f0cfd857d/actionpack/lib/action_dispatch/http/parameters.rb#L50
[Puma]: https://github.com/puma/puma/blob/1b302a5de07b974f08b20b87c86326ee0e57271d/lib/puma/server.rb#L557

issue_context.title: ActionDispatch(?) does not process multiple files when existing records are sent with the same request
issue_context.body:
### Steps to reproduce
```
class Product < ApplicationRecord
  has_many :images
  accepts_nested_attributes_for :images
end
```
```
class Image < ApplicationRecord
  has_one_attached :file
end
```

Now imagine the product form can change existing images and uploading new ones. For this I would have an input like
```
<input type"text" name="product[images_attributes][1][caption]" ?>
```
Be aware of the `[1]` to refer to an existing record, which will lead to the following params:
```
{"plant"=>{"images_attributes"=>{"1"=>{"caption"=>"new value"}}}}
```
If I would want to upload new images in the same request, I would need to create a file field which looks like this
```
<input multiple="multiple" type="file" name="product[images_attributes][2][file]" />
```
since using only `product[images_attributes][][file]` would try to create an array, which does not work with the existing record pattern from above.

### Expected behavior
When selecting multiple files in this scenario, multiple files get created and the existing image gets updated.

### Actual behavior
When selecting multiple files in this scenario, only the last file gets created and the existing image gets updated.

When only new images are created, using
```
<input multiple="multiple" type="file" name="product[images_attributes][][file]" />
```
is working and is creating multiple images correctly. (But cannot be used together with updating an existing record as described above)

### System configuration
**Rails version**: 6.0.3.2

**Ruby version**: 2.7.1p83 (2020-03-31 revision a0c7c23c9c) [x86_64-darwin19]

Thanks for the sample application. That helps a lot.

The problem here is that Rack is not unable to parse these parameters since, as you mentioned, one of them is an array and the other a hash:

```rb
parser = Rack::QueryParser.new(Rack::QueryParser::Params, 17, 4)

parser.parse_nested_query("product[images_attributes][][caption]=value")
#=> {"product"=>{"images_attributes"=>[{"caption"=>"value"}]}}

parser.parse_nested_query("product[images_attributes][0][caption]=value")
#=> {"product"=>{"images_attributes"=>{"0"=>{"caption"=>"value"}}}}

parser.parse_nested_query("product[images_attributes][][caption]=value&product[images_attributes][0][caption]=value")
#=> Rack::QueryParser::ParameterTypeError (expected Hash (got Array) for param `images_attributes')

parser.parse_nested_query("product[images_attributes][0][caption]=value&product[images_attributes][][caption]=value")
#=> Rack::QueryParser::ParameterTypeError (expected Array (got Rack::QueryParser::Params) for param `images_attributes')
```

`images_attributes` can't be both a hash and an array at the same time, so it makes sense to me that Rack would raise an error here.

You should be able to address this in your application by making sure you use an array all the time, perhaps like this:

```erb
<input multiple="multiple" type="file" name="product[images_attributes][<%= product.images.length %>][file]" id="product_images_attributes_files" />
```

---

I think there still may be a bug here though: your example is returning a 404 rather than a 400 for invalid params. If we make a `GET` request with similar params (.e.g /?product[]=a&product[0]=b), we do indeed get a 400 response. But in this case, since we aren't able to parse the params and identify this is a `PATCH` request (via the `_method` param), it gets treated as a `POST` and so we see an unexpected 404 `No route matches [POST] "/products/1"`.

You get a clue about this in the server logs (coming from the rack [method override middleware](https://github.com/rack/rack/blob/master/lib/rack/method_override.rb)):

```
Invalid or incomplete POST params                                                                                     
Started POST "/products/1"
```

whereas if things were working correctly we should have seen:

```
Started PATCH "/products/1"
```

I haven't delved deeply into the Action Dispatch code, so I can't offer an informed opinion at the moment.  A new middleware to validate the format for the params is an interesting approach.  My first thought would have been to make the current param parsing code raise a specific error that could be translated to a 400, but it sounds like the order of operations (i.e. when we resolve the route) might make that difficult?

You might still be able to get the desired behavior by using two totally separate fields, one for updating and another for the new files, then doing some extra work server side to turn them into what you need.
